messages:
elaine: Heads-up — after upgrading to python-sdk 0.9.0 our CI started failing with mypy errors coming from the autogenerated models. I think the generator changed some optional fields to Union[str, None] instead of Optional[str]?

matt: ugh. can you paste the error?

elaine: sure — minimal repro from the failing job:

```
src/app/clients/generated_models.py:142: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type 'str', variable has type 'Optional[str]')  [assignment]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 27 source files)
```

elaine: The generated dataclass has `name: Optional[str] = None` but the client code does `model.name = resp[\"name\"]` (which mypy infers as str). Before 0.9.0 we used TypedDict in the response stub so this didn't surface.

sergio: do we have runtime failures or just type-check failures?

elaine: only static typecheck so far. Tests pass. CI job runs mypy as a gating step for a few repos.

matt: sounds like a typing gap between generated response types and the model attr types. We changed the generator to prefer Pydantic BaseModel for models — maybe the response shapes are still typed as Mapping[str, Any].

elaine: exactly. quick patch I tried is to cast the resp access: `model.name = cast(Optional[str], resp.get(\"name\"))` but that's noisy to patch across callers. Would prefer SDK fix.

matt: filed #1584 to track — thanks. @sergio can the generator emit more precise response stubs (TypedDict) or mark assignments as type: ignore?

sergio: we can either 1) emit TypedDict for responses (best for mypy/pyright), 2) make model attributes Any, or 3) add a mypy plugin stub. TypedDict seems ideal but is more work. Any objections?

elaine: TypedDict would be lovely. Also some users run pyright which complains about Optional vs str too. So unified fix helps both.

matt: we should also consider `from __future__ import annotations` to avoid forward-ref issues and keep runtime cheap.

sergio: noted. I'll prototype TypedDict output in the generator branch. Will push a WIP PR later today.

devx-bot: CI for repo-redwood/python-sdk #246 started

matt: thanks — can we also add a short migration note in the changelog + an example showing how to opt into stricter types? e.g., `from redwood import types as rw_types` or similar.

elaine: yes pls. Also please consider an opt-in flag `--typed-responses` for the CLI generator so teams can opt in without breaking semver for default behavior.

sergio: good idea. I'll make it opt-in for the 0.9.x patch target and then flip default in 1.0.0.

elaine: perfect. one more nit — some generated models currently use `List[Any]` for embeddings; could we use `List[float]` when schema indicates numeric? caught a real user confusion where go SDK had stronger types.

sergio: will add heuristics. if schema says number -> use float. if ambiguous -> Any.

ci-bot: CI report: mypy job failed on branch fix/typed-responses (see https://ci.internal/246/mypy)

matt: cool — @sergio when you have WIP PR drop it here and I'll help with tests and adding an integration job that runs both mypy and pyright.

elaine: thanks all. saving a patch copy of quickcasts for the interim: `from typing import cast, Optional` then `model.name = cast(Optional[str], resp.get('name'))` — but we should avoid telling customers to litter their code with casts.

sergio: agreed. I'll aim for a PR with generator flag + unit tests covering mypy/pyright. ETA EOD PST.

matt: tagging this for devex follow-up: we should add a small sample app to the repo that demonstrates strong typing + mypy config. makes onboarding easier.

elaine: yes — sample app that uses typed responses + async client would be great. current sample only shows sync usage.

sergio: noted — adding async sample too. will include in PR description.

matt: thanks, folks. ping here when PR is up and I'll review. :thumbsup:
